summary: Context-only shadow deliberation: the measured tape remains risk-on (77) and the risk radar is calm, but the confirmed US Q2/Reflation label is weakly held (confidence 0.199) while its current axes read raw Q3/Stagflation signs (growth -0.333, inflation +0.24), now 2 of 7 confirmation sessions. Liquidity is contracting in an orderly, non-stressed drain: 20-day net liquidity is down $79.54bn, the RRP buffer is exhausted, and credit remains healthy. This is a regime-label and plumbing tension, not a signal or escalation. Factor evidence is immature: only 10 panel dates, no Pair G records, no factor-attention history, no scorecard survivors, and the composite is untradeable. The graded spine sample returned mostly unsigned-MFE board records, which cannot establish directional efficacy; kernel review leaves every cited engine unarmed. US-board signed excess has weakened in Q2, while radar and several desk families have negative signed excess over graded horizons. Four shadow attention items were recorded with pre-committed clearing criteria. No hypothesis was staked because the available observations do not support a sufficiently clean, non-originating pre-commitment.
what_fired: Confirmed Q2 label versus raw Q3 axes: pending Q3 confirmation is 2/7 sessions.
Risk-on tape versus orderly liquidity contraction: net liquidity -$79.54bn over 20 days with no confirming credit stress.
Confluence graph reports 34 ticker-level demand-versus-supply divergences; examples include IBM, VSAT, RKLB, and GOOG.
Open-thesis ledger contains numerous entries past their check_by dates that remain marked open.
contradictions_review: The committed graph contains a tension-level briefing-divergence contradiction covering 34 names. The options contradiction edge currently has n=0 and therefore supplies no name-level opposition. Pair G is dormant because the factor panel has only 10 dates, below its 60-date activation floor; absence here is lack of coverage, not agreement. The master-brain ledger also contains unresolved thesis hygiene conflicts: several China-equity, semiconductor, Bitcoin, Treasury, high-yield, and US-equity theses are still open after their evaluation dates. Current China/HK Q4 growth-scare states with contracting liquidity conflict with the still-open low-conviction China-overweight thesis sufficiently to deserve operator review, but not a directional conclusion. The current market backdrop does not itself falsify the growth-underweight thesis because IWF/IWD is only +1.16% over 20 days versus its pre-committed +5% relative-return gate.

Briefing demand/supply divergences — clear if the next contradiction read is zero or the 34-name set falls below 17 without replacement.
